title: Transparent Hugepage Defragmentation Stalls
exclusions: This host-level correlation does not measure stall duration, identify the stalled process, or prove that a particular Transparent Hugepage (THP) fault caused a particular compaction stall. `/proc/vmstat` counters are cumulative event counts, not milliseconds, pages, bytes, or percentages. A same-sample increase in `compact_stall` and THP fault counters is temporal evidence only; HugeTLB or other huge-page activity can also contribute to compaction, and unrelated activity can coincide within the 60-second sample interval. The search excludes counter resets, reboot boundaries, samples more than 180 seconds apart, unsupported collectors, and malformed values. It does not detect a silent host without an inventory-backed freshness control, replace process-level tracing or application latency telemetry, prescribe a THP policy, prove a kernel defect, or provide security or compliance evidence.
evidence: After deployment, retain the `UC-1.1.50 - Transparent Hugepage Defragmentation Stalls` saved-search definition and ACL, scheduler and triggered-alert history, each result row, and the corresponding raw `linux:thp:defrag` snapshots. A review package should also include the collector hash, effective `inputs.conf` and `props.conf`, a same-time comparison with `/proc/vmstat` and THP sysfs policy files, approved threshold and routing decisions, control-test inputs and outputs, and any time-bounded exception records. These artifacts show counter movement and host-level temporal correlation only. This documentation review did not create them or validate the use case in a running Splunk or Linux production environment.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, write two `event_type=thp_defrag_sample collection_status=ok` events 60 seconds apart for `host=thp-lab-01` and one `boot_id`. Use first/second values `compact_stall=20/21`, `compact_success=8/9`, `compact_fail=2/2`, `thp_fault_alloc=100/102`, and `thp_fault_fallback=10/11`, with `thp_enabled_policy=always`, `thp_defrag_policy=always`, and `khugepaged_defrag=1`. Run the SPL calculation with fixture time bounds. Expect one result with `correlated_compact_stall_delta=1`, `compact_stall_delta=1`, `thp_fault_attempt_delta=3`, `thp_fault_fallback_delta=1`, `thp_fault_fallback_pct=33.33`, `observed_seconds=60`, and `correlated_stalls_per_minute=1`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run four isolated variants and expect zero results: (1) increase `compact_stall` by one while leaving both THP fault counters unchanged; (2) increase `thp_fault_alloc` while leaving `compact_stall` unchanged; (3) place the two increasing samples under different `boot_id` values or decrease any required counter; and (4) separate otherwise positive samples by more than 180 seconds or set `collection_status=unsupported`. These variants prove the strict one-event boundary, required same-interval THP activity, reboot/reset protection, maximum correlation interval, and collector-status exclusion.

dataSources: One read-only scripted-input event per Linux host every 60 seconds from `/proc/vmstat`, `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`, `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag`, and `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/khugepaged/defrag`, routed to the deployment-local `index=os` and custom `sourcetype=linux:thp:defrag`. The event contract is `event_type=thp_defrag_sample`, `collection_status=ok`, string fields `boot_id`, `thp_enabled_policy`, and `thp_defrag_policy`, integer context field `khugepaged_defrag`, and cumulative integer event counters `compact_stall`, `compact_success`, `compact_fail`, `thp_fault_alloc`, and `thp_fault_fallback`. Splunk supplies `_time` and `host`; no standard syslog message or `Splunk_TA_nix` input supplies this contract.
app: A locally maintained collection app containing the documented scripted input and sourcetype settings. A Splunk Universal Forwarder can execute the script and transport stdout; no Splunkbase or premium app is required, and `Splunk_TA_nix` must not be credited with producing this custom event.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:thp:defrag" event_type="thp_defrag_sample" collection_status="ok" earliest=-21m@m latest=-5m@m
| addinfo
| fields _time host boot_id thp_enabled_policy thp_defrag_policy khugepaged_defrag compact_stall compact_success compact_fail thp_fault_alloc thp_fault_fallback info_min_time
| eval khugepaged_defrag=tonumber(khugepaged_defrag), compact_stall=tonumber(compact_stall), compact_success=tonumber(compact_success), compact_fail=tonumber(compact_fail), thp_fault_alloc=tonumber(thp_fault_alloc), thp_fault_fallback=tonumber(thp_fault_fallback)
| where isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(boot_id) AND isnotnull(thp_enabled_policy) AND isnotnull(thp_defrag_policy) AND in(khugepaged_defrag,0,1) AND compact_stall>=0 AND compact_success>=0 AND compact_fail>=0 AND thp_fault_alloc>=0 AND thp_fault_fallback>=0
| sort 0 host boot_id _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(_time) as previous_time last(compact_stall) as previous_compact_stall last(compact_success) as previous_compact_success last(compact_fail) as previous_compact_fail last(thp_fault_alloc) as previous_thp_fault_alloc last(thp_fault_fallback) as previous_thp_fault_fallback by host boot_id
| where isnotnull(previous_time) AND _time>previous_time AND _time-previous_time<=180 AND compact_stall>=previous_compact_stall AND compact_success>=previous_compact_success AND compact_fail>=previous_compact_fail AND thp_fault_alloc>=previous_thp_fault_alloc AND thp_fault_fallback>=previous_thp_fault_fallback
| eval sample_seconds=_time-previous_time, compact_stall_delta=compact_stall-previous_compact_stall, compact_success_delta=compact_success-previous_compact_success, compact_fail_delta=compact_fail-previous_compact_fail, thp_fault_alloc_delta=thp_fault_alloc-previous_thp_fault_alloc, thp_fault_fallback_delta=thp_fault_fallback-previous_thp_fault_fallback
| where _time>=info_min_time+60
| eval thp_fault_attempt_delta=thp_fault_alloc_delta+thp_fault_fallback_delta, correlated_compact_stall_delta=if(compact_stall_delta>0 AND thp_fault_attempt_delta>0,compact_stall_delta,0), correlated_interval=if(correlated_compact_stall_delta>0,1,0)
| stats sum(correlated_compact_stall_delta) as correlated_compact_stall_delta sum(compact_stall_delta) as compact_stall_delta sum(compact_success_delta) as compact_success_delta sum(compact_fail_delta) as compact_fail_delta sum(thp_fault_alloc_delta) as thp_fault_alloc_delta sum(thp_fault_fallback_delta) as thp_fault_fallback_delta sum(thp_fault_attempt_delta) as thp_fault_attempt_delta sum(correlated_interval) as correlated_intervals sum(sample_seconds) as observed_seconds count as sample_intervals earliest(_time) as window_start latest(_time) as window_end latest(thp_enabled_policy) as thp_enabled_policy latest(thp_defrag_policy) as thp_defrag_policy latest(khugepaged_defrag) as khugepaged_defrag by host boot_id
| eval thp_fault_fallback_pct=if(thp_fault_attempt_delta>0,round(100*thp_fault_fallback_delta/thp_fault_attempt_delta,2),null()), compaction_outcome_total=compact_success_delta+compact_fail_delta, compact_failure_pct=if(compaction_outcome_total>0,round(100*compact_fail_delta/compaction_outcome_total,2),null()), correlated_stalls_per_minute=round(60*correlated_compact_stall_delta/observed_seconds,3)
| where correlated_compact_stall_delta>=1
| convert ctime(window_start) ctime(window_end)
| table host boot_id window_start window_end observed_seconds sample_intervals correlated_intervals correlated_compact_stall_delta correlated_stalls_per_minute compact_stall_delta compact_success_delta compact_fail_delta compact_failure_pct thp_fault_attempt_delta thp_fault_alloc_delta thp_fault_fallback_delta thp_fault_fallback_pct thp_enabled_policy thp_defrag_policy khugepaged_defrag
| sort 0 - correlated_compact_stall_delta host
description: Reports a Linux host when `compact_stall` and at least one THP page-fault outcome counter both increase in the same valid polling interval. It calculates per-boot deltas, rates, and outcome percentages from cumulative `/proc/vmstat` values and carries the active THP sysfs policies into the result without claiming process attribution or elapsed stall time.
value: Synchronous memory compaction can add unpredictable latency to an allocating process. A narrowly scoped correlation between measured compaction stalls and contemporaneous THP fault activity gives platform and application teams a defensible starting point for latency triage, policy review, and controlled tracing while avoiding pages based on keyword logs or invented millisecond values.
implementation: Deploy the exact read-only collector at a 60-second interval, validate its cumulative counters and selected sysfs policies against the same host, and schedule the delta search every 15 minutes over the documented delayed window. Treat one correlated stall as an investigative threshold because Linux publishes no universal healthy count; baseline by workload class and require application-latency or controlled tracing evidence before paging or changing THP policy.
visualization: Use a host table with the alert fields and separate time-series panels for `correlated_compact_stall_delta`, `compact_stall_delta`, and `thp_fault_fallback_pct`; annotate policy and deployment changes. Label deltas as event counts, `correlated_stalls_per_minute` as events/minute, percentages as ratios of counter-event deltas, and `observed_seconds` as seconds. Pair with p95/p99 application latency and a separate inventory-backed collector-freshness panel. Never graph cumulative counters as rates or label any field as stall duration.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. `linux:thp:defrag` is a custom host metric contract with no claimed CIM data-model mapping; use the raw-event SPL.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved memory or THP stress test** — `stress-ng`, a benchmark, or a purpose-built allocator can create genuine compaction stalls and THP faults without an incident. Confirm the exact command, host set, owner, and approved start/end time; mute notification only for that bounded test while retaining samples.

2. **Expected database, virtual-machine, or JVM warm-up** — Rapid anonymous-memory population after a controlled restart can create a short correlated burst. Match the result to the deployment record and application p95/p99 latency. Use a documented warm-up routing policy, not a permanent host exclusion.

3. **Coincidental host-level activity** — The two counter families have no shared allocation ID. An explicit HugeTLB or other huge-page compaction stall can occur during the same 60-second sample in which an unrelated THP fault succeeds or falls back. Use controlled function tracing and the `mm_page_alloc` tracepoint when causal attribution is required; do not present this result as proof.

4. **Approved THP policy rollout** — Changing `enabled`, `defrag`, application `MADV_HUGEPAGE` behavior, or `khugepaged/defrag` can legitimately alter the counter pattern. Correlate the captured policy values with configuration management and the maintenance window, then compare pre/post workload latency before accepting a new baseline.

5. **Host class with routine latency-insensitive compaction** — Batch workers can exceed a one-event investigative threshold while meeting their service objective. Keep the sensitive result for trend analysis, but promote it to paging only with a reviewed host-class baseline, repeated affected windows, or a separate application-latency condition.

6. **Duplicate local scripted inputs** — Two stanzas can emit duplicate snapshots with identical or near-identical times and distort `observed_seconds` or interval counts. Compare `_raw`, `source`, and `splunk btool inputs list --debug`; remove the duplicate and rerun controls rather than suppressing the host.

If notification exceptions are necessary, implement a time-bound exception wrapper only after the documented calculation: `| lookup linux_thp_defrag_exceptions.csv host OUTPUT owner reason change_ticket valid_from valid_until`, parse both UTC bounds, and filter notification delivery with `| where isnull(valid_until_epoch) OR valid_from_epoch>now() OR valid_until_epoch<now()`. Key the lookup by exact `host`; reject wildcards, missing bounds, and expired entries. The base SPL intentionally contains no lookup, so an ungoverned file cannot silently change the portable detection contract.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and semantic boundary

Assign a Linux memory-performance owner, each workload's application owner, and a Splunk content owner. An approved event index must exist; this record calls it `os`, but the index is a deployment choice that must be changed consistently in the input and SPL. Run the collector locally through a Universal Forwarder or another approved Splunk scripted-input tier. The five source files are normally readable without elevated privileges, so do not grant root or permission to write THP controls merely for monitoring. Confirm the running kernel exposes all five named `/proc/vmstat` counters and the three THP sysfs files before rollout.

Linux defines `compact_stall` as incrementing whenever a process stalls to run memory compaction so that a huge page is free. It defines `compact_success` and `compact_fail` as compaction outcome event counts. `thp_fault_alloc` counts successful huge-page allocation and charge on a page fault; `thp_fault_fallback` counts a page fault that could not allocate or charge a huge page and used small pages instead. None is a timer. The collector therefore preserves integer counts, and the SPL subtracts adjacent snapshots; it never calls a counter value milliseconds or bytes. Linux recommends function tracing around `__alloc_pages()` and `mm_page_alloc` when duration and huge-allocation attribution are required.

The active `/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag` value is context, not an alert gate. `always` permits synchronous reclaim and compaction for eligible THP allocation failures; `defer` requests background reclaim/compaction; `madvise` limits direct work to advised regions; `defer+madvise` combines background behavior for ordinary regions with direct behavior for advised regions; and `never` avoids this defragmentation path when a huge page is not immediately available. Application advice, per-size THP settings on newer kernels, HugeTLB activity, and kernel implementation details mean a host result must still be investigated. `khugepaged/defrag` controls background khugepaged compaction and must not be described as an application-stall duration.

## 1. Configure the exact collector and field contract

Create an app such as `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_thp_defrag/`, place the reviewed `scriptExample` at `bin/collect_thp_defrag.sh`, make it executable, and keep it owned by the forwarder service account. The script is read-only. It extracts the bracketed active value from the two multi-choice sysfs files, reads the `khugepaged` zero/one switch and boot ID, and validates all counters as non-negative decimal integers. It emits one normal key-value line or one classified error line; it never substitutes zero for unavailable data.

Use this app-local `local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://./bin/collect_thp_defrag.sh]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
sourcetype = linux:thp:defrag
```

At 60 seconds, each host normally emits 1,440 small events per day. Keep the script-path `source` value for provenance. Configure the parsing tier for `[linux:thp:defrag]` with `SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false` and `DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT`; configure the search tier with `KV_MODE = auto`. The event has no embedded time because these are instantaneous snapshots: Splunk input time becomes `_time`, and input metadata supplies `host`. Do not emit a second host field, use index-time key-value extraction, or claim this sourcetype is supplied by `Splunk_TA_nix`.

Run the script manually as the forwarder account. For an `ok` event, compare every counter with `/proc/vmstat`, the UUID with `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, and each policy with the bracketed sysfs value. Confirm exactly one stdout line and no shell diagnostics. Then use `splunk btool inputs list --debug` to prove that only one enabled stanza owns the script. Route `collector_error` events to a separate data-quality search; `unsupported` means coverage is absent, not that counter activity is zero.

## 2. Validate ingestion before calculating deltas

Search 30 minutes of raw events and verify one normal sample per minute per host, allowing documented forwarding delay:

```spl
index=os sourcetype="linux:thp:defrag" earliest=-30m
| stats count as events latest(_time) as last_seen values(collection_status) as statuses dc(source) as sources by host
| eval expected_about=30
```

Inspect `_raw` for two hosts and confirm all `requiredFields` are populated. Use `timechart span=5m count by host limit=0` to expose gaps or duplicate inputs; a healthy 60-second collector normally contributes about five events to a complete five-minute bucket. Build a separate inventory-backed freshness rule because the primary search cannot return a host that has stopped sending data. Investigate after two missed polls plus the deployment's measured forwarding allowance.

Counter movement must be non-negative within one boot. A lower value under the same `boot_id` indicates malformed or mixed source data and is discarded. A changed boot ID starts a new epoch. The 180-second maximum adjacent-sample interval prevents a long collection outage from being represented as a tight temporal correlation; it is three times the intended poll interval, not a Linux threshold.

## 3. Create, schedule, and understand the alert

Save the primary SPL as `UC-1.1.50 - Transparent Hugepage Defragmentation Stalls`. Schedule it at minutes 5, 20, 35, and 50 with `5,20,35,50 * * * *`; trigger when result count is greater than zero. Its embedded `earliest=-21m@m latest=-5m@m` supplies one predecessor minute plus a complete delayed 15-minute evaluation window. `addinfo` exposes the dispatch lower bound, and the `_time>=info_min_time+60` clause removes the predecessor-only minute after it has seeded the first delta. Adjacent scheduled windows therefore evaluate new intervals while allowing five minutes for ingestion.

**Understanding this SPL:** Numeric conversion and validity checks reject missing or impossible values. Sorting and `streamstats current=f window=1` attach each host/boot snapshot's immediately preceding values. Reboot grouping, monotonic checks, and the 180-second gap limit protect subtraction. `thp_fault_attempt_delta` is the sum of successful fault allocation/charge events and fallback events; `thp_fault_fallback_pct` is fallback events divided by those two documented outcome counts. `compact_failure_pct` is a ratio of `compact_fail` to success-plus-fail outcome events. Both are percentages of event deltas, not percentages of memory or elapsed time.

The portable investigative threshold is `correlated_compact_stall_delta>=1`: at least one `compact_stall` increase occurred in an adjacent sample that also had at least one THP fault outcome. The threshold is exactly one because it tests event presence; neither Linux nor Splunk defines a universally healthy per-window count. `correlated_stalls_per_minute` normalizes only those correlated stall events by observed sample seconds. The result also carries total `compact_stall_delta`, which can include uncorrelated intervals. Before enabling paging, report without the final `where` for at least seven representative days, segment by workload class, and obtain approval for persistence, rate, or latency corroboration. Do not change the core rule to `count>5`, relabel counts as milliseconds, or infer causality from same-host timing.

## 4. Execute controls and investigate safely

Run both `controlTest` narratives with timestamps inside explicit fixture bounds. The positive arithmetic must match exactly, including the 33.33-percent fallback ratio and one event/minute normalized rate. The negative variants must prove both sides of the conjunction, boot/reset handling, gap rejection, and unsupported-source rejection. Add a boundary case with `compact_stall` unchanged and confirm the strict `>=1` result threshold does not fire. Preserve the fixture events, time bounds, SPL revision, and outputs.

On a representative lab host, capture the source files, collector stdout, and indexed event within one polling interval. Values must match exactly; policy strings must equal the bracketed selections. Do not induce compaction on a production host merely to make an alert. If an approved workload test naturally moves the counters, compare the result with application latency. For causal or duration analysis, Linux's documented tracing approach belongs in a controlled diagnostic session owned by the kernel/performance team; continuous high-volume tracing is not part of this collection contract.

## 5. Operationalize, troubleshoot, and retain evidence

Build the panels described in `visualization` from valid snapshots and saved-search results. Keep event counts, event/minute rates, percentages, and seconds on correctly labeled axes. Display `thp_enabled_policy`, `thp_defrag_policy`, and `khugepaged_defrag` as context and annotate configuration or workload deployments. Route initial results to the platform-performance queue, throttle duplicate notifications by host for 60 minutes, and require latency or service-impact confirmation before incident escalation.

The runbook should first confirm sample continuity, boot ID, counter monotonicity, and active policy; then check planned tests, service restarts, and configuration changes. Compare `compact_success_delta` and `compact_fail_delta`, but remember they are outcomes rather than duration. Review memory pressure, swap behavior, and application p95/p99 latency. Any THP policy change can trade throughput, memory consumption, and latency and must follow workload testing and change control; this alert must never write sysfs.

No events from one host: verify app deployment, execute permission, source-file readability, index routing, and scripted-input messages in `splunkd.log`. `collection_status=unsupported`: inspect the exact missing kernel interface and keep the host in a coverage report. Null fields: inspect `_raw` and effective search-tier `KV_MODE`. Negative deltas: verify boot ID and eliminate mixed collectors. Duplicate or sub-second samples: use `btool` and `source` to find overlapping stanzas. Large deltas after a gap: confirm the 180-second guard is present. An alert with no user-visible delay can be valid because the counter contains no duration; tune routing from measured service behavior rather than suppressing evidence.

Retain raw snapshots, search exports, dispatch and alert records, collector and configuration hashes, source comparisons, threshold approval, tests, and exception records according to the operational retention policy. Suppression may mute a notification, but it must not delete source samples or disguise collector freshness.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for times when a Linux server pauses work to rearrange memory while programs are asking for larger memory blocks. The signal helps the team investigate slowdowns, but it cannot say which program paused or how long the pause lasted.
reviewer: Cursor AI documentation review against Linux kernel and Splunk primary sources; no runtime or SME validation

cost.search_load_notes: One small 60-second snapshot per host and a scheduled raw-event delta search over a delayed 16-minute input range; no joins, subsearches, real-time scheduling, or acceleration.
